newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico eases prison crowds after tunnel found.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico eases prison crowds after tunnel found.

text.p: New Mexico officials rushed to ease dangerous overcrowding in its prison system on Friday after unearthing a 30-foot (9 metre) escape tunnel and plans for a riot at the state penitentiary.

Authorities said they would transfer 256 prisoners next week to a private facility in Arizona, and extended a 3-day-old lockdown at the state penitentiary near Santa Fe where a violent escape plan was discovered earlier this week.

Under the plan, prisoners were preparing to start a riot which would cover their escape through the tunnel, although officials said the tunnel was still 60 feet (18 metres) short of reaching the penitentiary fence. The jail was the site of a 1980 riot which killed 33 inmates.

Gov. Gary Johnson said transferring some prisoners to Arizona would help ease pressure on state jails but he is also urging state legislators to provide funding for additional prison facilities to house 2,400 inmates.
"This is just a quick fix," he said. "We need a longer term solution."
New Mexico's state prison system currently holds 4,700 inmates, about 1,000 more than it was designed to house.
State legislators on Thursday passed a bill which would allow the early release of non-violent felons when prison overcrowding reaches critical levels.
Legislators have allocated $500,000 for the immediate transfer of prisoners to Arizona.
